$comment-bootstrap: v0.10.0 was cut by hand in 1b418ec (CHANGELOG section, hatch fallback-version) and never tagged — the only tag on origin is v0.9.0. bootstrap-sha anchors release-please's first run at that cut so the first release PR carries what landed since 0.10.0, not the whole history. Tagging v0.10.0 at 1b418ec is a human act (release.yml publishes on a tag push) and is left to the operator.

..$comment-extra-files: pyproject.toml carries no static version (hatch-vcs derives it from the tag, and release-please's python updater skips a dynamic version with a warning), but two files do carry the number and release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with either: the hatch fallback-version, which tests/test_version_changelog_sync.py holds equal to CHANGELOG.md's newest release, and safe-app-manifest.json's version. Both are bumped in the release PR.
..$comment-what-cuts-a-release: EVERY type listed above without "hidden": true cuts a release on its own — not just feat and fix. jeles learned this the expensive way: v0.4.1 was tagged and published to PyPI for a single ci: commit that changed a workflow file and nothing a user installs. That is survivable while release PRs are merged by hand, because you see what is in them; release-please.yml here arms auto-merge, so an un-hidden type ships to PyPI unattended, and a PyPI version can never be reused. The set is the fleet's (tests/fleet_conventions.json, release_cutting_types) and tests/test_fleet_conventions.py holds this file to it.
..$comment-hidden-rule: The line is: does this commit change what someone gets from `pip install willows-grove`? docs/test/ci/chore do not — tests and workflows are not packaged, and a README edit only moves the PyPI page — so they are hidden and ride along with the next real release. build and deps stay visible because a dependency or packaging change genuinely alters the installed artifact, and hiding them would mean a dependency fix never reaching anyone, silently. refactor and perf stay visible because they change shipped code, and a version number is what you point at when a refactor turns out to have broken something. Hidden also means absent from the generated CHANGELOG section — release-please has no 'list it but do not release on it' setting, so this is a real trade, taken deliberately; the hand-written [Unreleased] bullets INVARIANTS.md §3 requires are the record of hidden work. The set is the fleet's (tests/fleet_conventions.json, hidden_types).
..$comment-changelog-shape: CHANGELOG.md is hand-written Keep-a-Changelog with a [Unreleased] section that INVARIANTS.md §3 requires every code PR to append to. release-please inserts its generated section before the first '## [' heading it finds, which is [Unreleased], so a release section lands above the unreleased notes rather than absorbing them; and the release PR's own commit carries no Persona: trailer and touches safe-app-manifest.json, so INVARIANTS.md §11 and §3's checkers reject it as written. Both are governance questions, proposed on PR #61, not settled here.
